headlines: CoreWeave to Participate in the 2026 UBS Global Technology and AI Conference (StockTitan, 2026-11-23)
CoreWeave Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results (StockTitan, 2026-11-10)
gappers.catalyst_detail: There is no CRWV-specific news on Nov 24 or Nov 25. The last company release is a Nov 23 conference-participation notice, and the last substantive one is Q3 results on Nov 10. What is actually moving the stock is the AI-infrastructure complex repricing: Nasdaq-100 futures are -1.4% pre-open, VIX spot is 29.21 (+10.81%, Cboe), Ambarella fell 37% after Tuesday's close on Q4 revenue guidance of $70-75M against ~$112M consensus, and Nov 24 saw Micron -11%, AMD -8.9%, Intel -8.1%, NVDA -5.86%. CRWV's Q3 print itself supplies the bear case: revenue tripled to $3.661B and operating income reached $207M, but the net loss WIDENED to $709M because net interest expense hit $846M, with Q4 interest guided to $1.05-1.15B against $37-39B of planned capex.
gappers.why: A debt-funded, pre-profit infrastructure buildout is a long-duration asset, and its equity is the first thing repriced when risk appetite and the AI demand narrative crack together. CRWV's interest expense now exceeds its operating income by roughly 4x and the buildout is financed with ~$4.2B of convertible notes, a $2.6B facility and a new program to sell up to 35M Class A shares — so the market is marking the financing risk, not the $132.5B backlog. Ambarella's guide is a demand-side datapoint rather than a sentiment one, which is why it transmitted straight through the complex.
gappers.impact: Reads as a continuation of a confirmed downtrend, not a one-day headline spike that mean-reverts. Nov 24 volume was 2.09M, 1.24x the 20-day average — the only above-average print of the four, so CRWV is the name actually being distributed. At $39.75 the stock is just +1.2% above the Nov 20 52-week low of $39.29 and -36% from the Nov 11 high of $62.02; the +28% Nov 23 bounce on Huang's reinstatement fully retraced in two sessions, which is a failed-bounce/lower-high rejection rather than a base. Sector read-through is total: NBIS, BE and AMKR are all gapping -5% to -6.5% on the same tape with no news of their own.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Headline- and factor-driven with no durable thesis on this timeframe; the structural overhang (interest expense above operating income) is a multi-quarter problem, not a days-to-weeks catalyst, and the rulebook's sector table reads late-cycle, which does not favour Technology.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace — 0 open positions, 0% deployed, weekly trade count 0/3. The binding constraint is the gate itself, and it fails on arithmetic: at ATR14 16.73% the mandated 10% trailing stop sits only 0.60 ATR below spot, inside a single day's normal range, so it would be taken out by noise; the +20% target that 2:1 R:R requires is just 1.20 ATR away. Price is 54.6% below its 200-SMA, so the long-bias filter fails independently. It cannot clear 2:1 at any sane stop distance. Research only — no order.

headlines: Nebius Group (NBIS) PT Lowered to $200 at Baird (StreetInsider, 2026-11-23)
Nebius Group (NBIS) PT Lowered to $245 at Truist Securities (StreetInsider, 2026-11-21)
Nebius reports third quarter 2026 financial results (StockTitan, 2026-11-12)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No Nebius release has landed since the Nov 12 Q3 report, which itself closed -16.84% on the day. The only fresh single-name news is two price-target cuts in the last four sessions, both of which remain far above spot — the sell-side is chasing the price down rather than leading it, so these are confirmation, not cause. The Q3 numbers frame the risk: revenue rose 571% year-over-year to $980.8M with adjusted EBITDA of $465.8M and operating income turning positive at $50.4M, but non-current debt went from $4.103B to $14.003B, quarterly purchases of property, equipment and intangibles reached $7.300B, and operating cash flow was a $273.0M outflow. The $3.5B Citi facility secured Oct 22 is 364-day paper at Term SOFR plus 2.75%, rising to as much as 3.50%.
gappers.why: The mechanism is the same as CRWV's and it is a funding-structure story, not a demand story: short-dated, floating-rate debt financing a long-dated buildout. In a risk-off tape with VIX at 29 and the 10-year at a two-week low, the market reprices refinancing risk on a 364-day facility and the equity takes the adjustment, which is why the move is happening despite more than $40B of disclosed long-term contracts and a 571% revenue growth rate. High beta to the AI complex does the rest.
gappers.impact: Mixed, and the volume argues against panic. Nov 24 volume was 745k, only 0.92x the 20-day average, versus 1.54M on the Nov 20 capitulation low — so this leg down is drift on below-average participation rather than liquidation, which is the more constructive of the two readings for an eventual double bottom. But at $81.61 the stock sits barely above the Nov 20 low of $80.68 and is -49% from the Nov 11 high of $160.18, so the retest is live and unresolved. It remains +11.0% above the 52-week low of $73.53, slightly more cushion than CRWV or AMKR. Chart shape is identical to the other three — the same single factor.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Factor- and funding-driven with the Nov 20 low still being retested; no structural catalyst has changed since Nov 12, and the two analyst actions in hand are both downgrades to targets, which is not a thesis to buy into.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace — 0 positions, 0/3 weekly trades used. NBIS is the worst of the four on the stop arithmetic: ATR14 is 21.15% of price, so the mandated 10% trailing stop sits just 0.47 ATR below spot and would be hit by roughly half a normal day's range, while the +20% 2:1 target is only 0.95 ATR away. Price is 54.6% below its 200-SMA, failing the long filter independently. There is no stop distance that satisfies both the 10% rule and 2:1 R:R here. Research only — no order.

headlines: Bloom Energy (BE) Surges 21% on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Return (MarketWatch, Nov 2026)
Bloom Energy Gains Morgan Stanley Backing on Gigawatt Deployment (Google Finance listing)
Bloom Energy Reports Record Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Raises Full Year 2026 Guidance (StockTitan, 2026-10-22)
gappers.catalyst_detail: There is no negative company news. The last BE release is a Nov 20 community donation, and the fundamental record is the strongest of the four: Q3 revenue of $1,235.8M (+138.1% year-over-year) with product revenue +179.4%, GAAP gross margin 33.8%, operating income $225.4M against $7.8M a year earlier, net income $250.3M and diluted EPS $0.78, full-year 2026 guidance raised to $4.4-4.6B revenue and $3.10-3.40 non-GAAP EPS, cash of $2.487B, and admission to the S&P 500. Commercially it holds a 900MW onsite-power agreement with NTT DATA — its largest international project — plus Oracle's stated intent to procure up to 2.8GW. What happened instead is that the Nov 23 Huang-return spike, worth +21% to +27% in a session, has been given back over Nov 24-25 alongside the rest of the complex.
gappers.why: This is a valuation and duration unwind rather than an earnings problem. At $146.55 against 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $3.10-3.40 the stock trades near 43-47x forward earnings, and essentially all of the NTT DATA 900MW revenue ships from 2027 onward. A multiple that high resting on 2027-plus cash flows is the most rate- and sentiment-sensitive cohort in the market, so with QQQ 6.6% below its 200-SMA, VIX at 29 and a PCE print pending, the multiple compresses regardless of how good the last print was. The Huang headline inflated it on no change to fundamentals; the same absence of fundamental change deflates it.
gappers.impact: Looks like continued mean-reversion of a headline spike rather than a fundamental break, and the volume supports that: Nov 24 traded 506k, 0.90x the 20-day average, the same below-average drift signature as NBIS and well under the 1.12M on the Nov 20 low. At $146.55 the stock is +4.1% above the Nov 20 low of $140.73, -33% from the Nov 11 high of $217.76, but still +93.5% above its 52-week low of $75.75 — of the four it has given back the least and has the most air beneath it. Sector read-through runs both ways: BE's own Nov 12 sector release bundled GE Vernova, Constellation, Talen and Quanta, and TLN is the name that carried the dated $349-356 limit plan in the Nov 18-20 handoff.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The gap itself is the unwind of a two-day sentiment spike, so short-term; the NTT DATA and Oracle contracts are genuinely structural but ship from 2027, which is too far out to support a multi-day swing entry into a falling tape ahead of PCE.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace — 0 positions, 0/3 weekly trades used, so this would not crowd out an existing holding or a higher-ranked gapper (all three above it fail the same gate). It fails anyway: ATR14 is 14.63% of price, so the mandated 10% trailing stop sits 0.68 ATR below spot, inside one day's range, and price is 34.6% below its 200-SMA — the shallowest breach of the four but still a clear long-filter fail. Worth naming as the first candidate to revisit if the operator ever approves an ATR-based stop, because the fundamentals are real, the drawdown is the mildest and the 52-week-low cushion is the largest. Research only — no order.

Amkor Technology to Present at Upcoming Conferences (StockTitan, 2026-11-16)
Amkor Technology price target lowered to $38 from $41 at B. Riley (TipRanks, 2026-11-09)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nothing company-specific is driving this. The newest AMKR release is a Nov 18 dividend increase of less than a tenth of a cent, and the only analyst action in the window is B. Riley trimming its target to $38 from $41 on Nov 9. The move is transmitted from the semis complex — Nov 24 brought Micron -11%, AMD -8.9%, Intel -8.1% and NVDA -5.86%, and Ambarella then guided Q4 revenue to $70-75M against ~$112M consensus and fell 37% after the close. Layered on top is the pending US announcement of raised tariffs on China, the EU and 14 other economies, which lands directly on AMKR because its manufacturing footprint is Korea- and Asia-heavy. CNBC confirms the 52-week low of $29.95 was set on Nov 20 and today's pre-market print of $29.94-$30.17 is right back on it.
gappers.why: AMKR is the highest-beta transmission line in the group at beta 2.43 and the purest outsourced-assembly-and-test read on AI packaging demand, so a demand-side datapoint anywhere in accelerated computing hits it with amplification. Ambarella's guide and the Nov 24 memory and logic selloff are datapoints about exactly the advanced-packaging volumes AMKR is building $12B of Arizona capacity against, and tariff headlines compound it by threatening the cost base of its Asian footprint. The market is discounting the forward volume assumption, not the delivered quarter.
gappers.impact: Most likely to mean-revert of the four, because the gap is not volume-confirmed: Nov 24 traded 129k, just 0.68x the 20-day average and the lightest participation in the group, and pre-market volume is only about 35k shares against a 10-day average of 3.62M. A -5% gap on 35k shares is a thin-book quote, not distribution. The dissonance worth flagging is valuation: forward P/E 12.18, trailing P/E 12.82, Q3 net income $191M on $1.991B revenue, 18.3% gross margin, $2.4B cash against $2.5B debt, and $3B of NVIDIA prepayment agreements across Arizona and South Korea — the cheapest fundamentals of the four sitting on the deepest drawdown at -68.7% from the 52-week high. Sector read-through: it is the tariff- and demand-exposed leg of the same single factor.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The gap itself is an unconfirmed thin-book move with no company catalyst, so short-term; AMKR is nonetheless the one name of the four to carry forward as a LONG_TERM watch candidate, because the NVIDIA prepayment contracts and 12x forward earnings are structural and it is the only one of the four whose ATR sits inside the rulebook's viable 5-10% band.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace — 0 positions, 0/3 weekly trades used. AMKR is the only one of the four where the geometry nearly works: at ATR14 9.86% the mandated 10% trailing stop sits 1.01 ATR below spot, just outside one day's range, and the +20% target that 2:1 requires is 2.03 ATR away, which is reachable on a swing horizon. It still fails the long filter decisively — price is 46.2% below its 200-SMA, and that 200-SMA at $56.03 sits 86% above spot, so a trend reclaim is not a near-term event. Taking it would spend one of three weekly slots on a name in a confirmed downtrend, ahead of a PCE print whose release time this session could not confirm and a pending tariff announcement, into pre-Thanksgiving liquidity. Research only — no order.
